# Proverbs 25 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** These also [are]-proverbs-of Solomon, which [the]-men-of Hezekiah king-of Judah copied:

**2** Glory-of God [is] to-conceal a-matter, but-glory-of kings [is] to-search-out a-matter.

**3** [The]-heavens for-height and-[the]-earth for-depth, and-[the]-heart-of kings — there-is-no-searching.

**4** Remove dross from-silver, and-there-comes-out for-[the]-refiner a-vessel.

**5** Remove [the]-wicked before a-king, and-his-throne will-be-established in-righteousness.

**6** Do-not-honor-yourself before a-king, and-in-[the]-place-of great-ones do-not-stand,

**7** For better [is it]-said to-you, 'Come-up here,' than-[to]-be-brought-low before a-noble whom your-eyes have-seen.

**8** Do-not-go-out to-contend hastily, lest — what will-you-do in-its-end, when-your-neighbor puts-you-to-shame?

**9** Your-case plead with-your-neighbor, but-[the]-secret-of another do-not-reveal,

**10** Lest [the]-one-hearing puts-you-to-shame, and-your-evil-report does-not-return.

**11** Apples-of gold in-settings-of silver — a-word spoken upon its-circumstances.

**12** A-ring-of gold and-an-ornament-of fine-gold — a-reprover wise upon an-ear listening.

**13** Like-[the]-coolness-of snow in-[the]-day-of harvest [is] a-messenger faithful to-those-sending-him; and-[the]-soul-of his-masters he-refreshes.

**14** Clouds and-wind and-rain there-is-none — a-man boasting in-a-gift-of falsehood.

**15** By-patience a-ruler is-persuaded, and-a-tongue gentle breaks a-bone.

**16** Honey you-have-found — eat your-sufficiency, lest you-be-surfeited-of-it and-vomit-it.

**17** Make-rare your-foot from-[the]-house-of your-neighbor, lest he-be-surfeited-of-you and-hate-you.

**18** A-war-club and-a-sword and-an-arrow sharpened — a-man bearing against his-neighbor witness-of falsehood.

**19** A-tooth broken and-a-foot slipping — trust in-a-treacherous-one in-[the]-day-of distress.

**20** One-removing a-garment on-a-day-of cold, vinegar upon natron — so [is one]-singing songs upon a-heart evil.

**21** If your-enemy is-hungry give-him bread to-eat, and-if he-is-thirsty give-him water to-drink,

**22** For coals you [are]-heaping upon his-head, and-YHWH will-repay you.

**23** A-wind-of north brings-forth rain, and-a-face angry — a-tongue-of secrecy.

**24** Better to-dwell upon a-corner-of a-roof, than-a-woman-of contentions and-a-house-of sharing.

**25** Water cold upon a-soul weary — [so is] a-report good from-a-land far.

**26** A-spring muddied and-a-fountain ruined — a-righteous-one tottering before [the]-wicked.

**27** To-eat honey much [is]-not good, but-searching-out their-glory [is] glory.

**28** A-city broken-through without a-wall — a-man who-has-no restraint for-his-spirit.

---
## EMET Literal Notes

- **25:1**: Anshei Chizkiyah — 'men of Hezekiah.' Court scribes (c. 8th century BCE) who copied/compiled earlier Solomonic material. A rare editorial note documenting textual transmission.

- **25:11**: Tappukhei zahav be-maskiyyot kesef — 'apples of gold in settings of silver.' One of the most beautiful images in Proverbs. Tappukhei may be apples, apricots, or citrons.

- **25:21-22**: Feeding the enemy and heaping coals — cited by Paul in Romans 12:20. The 'coals' may refer to an Egyptian penitential ritual of carrying coals on the head as a sign of contrition.

— EMET
